Proposed: Mainz
research:
The archival abstract identifies Dr. Hermann Rosenberg as scholaster of Mariengreden and Mainz vicar general when he authenticated a royal charter. His office and contemporaneous colleagues connect him with the same scholaster in 1444-07-06.json and 1449-03-29.json. Bauer (bauer_1872.json) could not place the 1452 scholaster and vicar general in the Franken genealogy and considered non-noble origin possible. The Mainz patrician family is another possibility, but no kinship links him to it. His Mainz office and surname alone do not distinguish either family. The 1449 archiepiscopal register corroborates his office and colleagues: https://www.ingrossaturbuecher.de/index.php?cHash=346098438fe451949fb23ed021a533c4&id=380&tx_hisodat_sources%5Baction%5D=show&tx_hisodat_sources%5Bcontroller%5D=Sources&tx_hisodat_sources%5Bsource%5D=22092. Attribution unresolved.

Further research supports Mainz. F. W. E. Roth identifies Hermann, the canon-law doctor, Mariengreden scholaster and vicar general, as a member of the Mainz patrician Rosenberg family (Archiv für katholisches Kirchenrecht 80, 1900, pp. 189–192, https://archive.org/details/ArchivFuerKatholischesKirchenrecht1900/page/n191/mode/1up). The Erfurt matriculation of Easter 1425 groups Hermanus and Iacobus Rosenberg as de Maguncia (Weissenborn I, p. 131, https://archive.org/details/11698564bsb/page/n162/mode/1up), and the Repertorium Academicum Germanicum lists Hermann as a Mainz patrician (https://resource.database.rag-online.org/ngLB2O476LT2xahbfLkaw). Acta Cusana no. 2064 also records Eberhard Rumelfels of Forchheim as his sworn scribe in the 1451 synodal materials (https://actacusana.de/quellenverzeichnis/2064.pdf). His exact kinship within the Mainz family remains open.

entries.german: Dr. Hermann Rosenberg, Scholaster des Mainzer Mariengredenstifts und Generalvikar des Mainzer Erzbischofs Dietrich, vidimiert auf Bitten des Herzogs Stephan von Bayern die inserierte Urkunde König Friedrichs III. vom 5. August 1442, mit welcher dem Mainzer Klerus Schutz- und Rechtsprivilegien bestätigt werden. Zeugen: Konrad von Bensheim und Rudolf von Seligenstadt. Notarielle Bestätigung durch den kaiserlichen Notar Eberhard Rumelfels von Forchheim.
entries.english: Dr. Herman von Rosenberg, scholaster of the Mainz Mariengredenstift and vicar general of Archbishop Dietrich of Mainz, produced an authenticated copy, at the request of Duke Stephan of Bavaria, of King Friedrich III’s 5 August 1442 charter confirming legal protections and privileges for Mainz’s clergy. Konrad von Bensheim and Rudolf von Seligenstadt were witnesses. Imperial notary Eberhard Rumelfels of Forchheim certified the document.

facts.content: authenticated, at the request of Duke Stephan of Bavaria, a copy of King Friedrich III’s 5 August 1442 charter confirming privileges for Mainz’s clergy.
